title: Kitchen Science
intro: Boiling, rising and fizzing: the science you can find on any counter. Have a guess.

questions.prompt: At sea level, at what temperature does water boil?
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level. Higher up, where the air pressure is lower, it boils at a slightly lower temperature.

choices: Yeast makes tiny bubbles of gas
Air is pumped in by kneading alone
questions.explanation: Yeast feeds on sugars in the dough and releases carbon dioxide gas. The gas is trapped in the dough and puffs it up.

questions.prompt: Why is salt spread on icy paths?
choices: It lowers the temperature at which water freezes
questions.explanation: Salty water freezes at a lower temperature than fresh water, so salt helps ice melt when it is only a little below zero.

questions.prompt: Why does oil float on water?
choices: Oil is lighter for its size, which means less dense
Water pushes it up with bubbles
questions.explanation: Oil is less dense than water, so a given amount of oil weighs less and floats on top.

questions.prompt: What makes the fizz when you mix baking soda with vinegar?
questions.explanation: The baking soda and the acid in vinegar react to make carbon dioxide, and the gas forms the bubbles.

questions.prompt: Why do chopped onions make some people's eyes water?
choices: They give off a gas that irritates the eyes
questions.explanation: Cutting an onion breaks its cells and releases a sulphur-containing gas. Your eyes make tears to wash it away.

questions.prompt: Why does an ice cube float in a glass of water?
choices: Ice is less dense than liquid water
Ice is full of air holes only
Cold water is lighter than warm water
questions.explanation: Water expands a little as it freezes, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats with part of it above the surface.

questions.prompt: What is the browning on toast and on seared food mostly due to?
choices: A reaction between sugars and proteins when heated
questions.explanation: It is called the Maillard reaction. Heat makes sugars and amino acids react, creating new colours and flavours.

questions.prompt: Why does a lid help a pot of water boil sooner?
choices: It traps heat so less of it is lost
It adds pressure to the stove
It cools the water down first
questions.explanation: The lid holds in heat and steam, so the water warms faster and less energy is wasted.

questions.prompt: Why does a metal spoon in hot soup get hot faster than a wooden one?
choices: Metal carries heat along it better
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat, so warmth travels quickly along the handle. Wood is a poor conductor.

questions.prompt: What gets trapped in egg whites when you whisk them?
questions.explanation: Whisking folds air into the egg white proteins, which hold the bubbles and turn the liquid into foam.
